name: planner-sprints
notes: Planner → sprint loop with a feature list (T6; Anthropic's long-running harness). A person approves the plan; each sprint takes one failing feature, the engine runs the tests, a fresh critic on another family drives the result. Edit `run` to this project's end-to-end test command. When eval claims the plan complete, Jev grades the whole change against @code-change (the per-sprint verdict stays the critic's: Jev's whole-goal lines would fail every sprint until the last); a fail sends one more sprint, unsure goes to you. features.json is not hash-protected: plan writes it and eval flips its passes, so a hash taken at the start would fail every sprint's tests; the sprint task tells the builder not to change it.

nodes.task: Expand {goal} into SPEC.md and features.json ([{id, desc, passes: false}]). Ambitious scope, no low-level technology choices. Claim with both files.

Read the shared notes, git log and features.json. Take ONE failing feature, implement it with an end-to-end test, commit, and append one progress line to the notes. Do not change features.json: the evaluator flips passes.
Drive the result against SPEC.md. Claim `win` if this sprint's feature now works, `fail` with what must be fixed, or `route:complete` if every feature in features.json works.
